title: pm-dispatch skill: for p1 cards the L1 review thread starts the isolated L2 in parallel with L1
body:
repo:objectstack#1 · os-sales · session_01L6bhgUkbQqRUUFSiu2HGob

## Problem

`references/contract-review.md:18` says the dispatching seat runs the contract review (「谁跑 = 派发席,档经子代理或卡线程取」). In a project, that serialises the two reviews: the card thread hands back, L1 runs, and only then does the seat or card thread start the isolated L2. Each wait costs a wake and a full context re-read.

## Ruling

The maintainer ruled the lean flow for every p1 card. The ruling record is the first comment on this card; the PR's `Ruling-ref:` cites it.

## What changes

- `references/contract-review.md:18`: for a p1 card dispatched to a card thread, the L1 review thread starts the isolated L2 sub-agent at the same time as its L1, only when the card owes L2. The template brief is still posted before the record; independence and tier evidence are unchanged. Both opinions go back to the seat together, and the seat adopts the L2 record as today.
- `references/dispatch-runbook.md`, card-thread section: the same hand-back path in one line, and the card thread builds itself with no `os-dev` sub-agent (it already reads `os-dev.md`, the order, the card and its comments, not `SKILL.md`; keep that).
- The L1 lane file that names what the L1 thread does (`references/lanes/l1-review.md` or wherever the L1 thread's duties live): add the L2 start.
- Nothing else changes: the seat still claims, adopts, lands and closes out; S cards still run as sub-agents per #35784.

## Constraints

- `.claude/**` is governed: `Rule-change: ruled`, one `Ruling-ref:` line; the L2 record must read `Rule-change-verified: ruled`.
- Byte ratchet at headroom 0: compress the same file first; a raise needs the ruling record id and the measured delta per file.

## Done when

- `contract-review.md` and the card-thread section name the L1 thread as the L2 starter for p1 card-thread cards, running in parallel with L1.
- `check-skill-line-ratchet.mjs` passes.
